description: Monster Hunt bosses B (phase 8 family 11): thirteen encounters of The Witchwood's Monster Hunt with a clickable hero power (Splintergraft, Brushwood Centurion, Baran the Blind, Gravekeeper Damph, Doctor Sezavo, Garrow, the Rancorous, Crooked Pete, Cragtorr, Azalina Soulthief, Face Collector, Raeth Ghostsong, Grum, Gustave, the Gutripper), Crooked Pete's form change into Beastly Pete, and their boss-only cards. Boss deck lists are transcribed from hearthstone.wiki.gg boss pages (read 2026-11-14), by card name; tools/dungeon-run-catalog (step 'encounters') resolves the names against facts/violet-hold-2026-09.json, checks every card and writes data/dungeon-run/encounters-v1.json. The tier is the printed Health of the hero card (20: tier 1; 30: tier 2; 35 and 40: tier 3; 50 and 60: tier 4).
method: Each boss page was read as wikitext (?action=raw) and its one deck table transcribed in table order with the table's own counts (Crooked Pete's page has two tables, Crooked Pete and Beastly Pete); every table sums to 30 except Gravekeeper Damph's and Doctor Sezavo's (20 each). Face Collector's page has no table ("This boss plays a deck identical to the player's"). Boss-only cards carry their id; the wiki's row name "Witchwood's Touch (2)" is written as the card's name with its id, and "Spore Hallucination" (Crooked Pete), the wiki's current name of the card the client data still calls Hallucination (dbf 42011), carries the id UNG_856. Rules beyond the card texts come from the pages' Notes (Crooked Pete) and the Monster Hunt page's boss table (read 2026-11-14); what a text leaves open is decided in the row's adaptation notes. Generated by verify/tools/gen/p8f11/make_f11.py.

adaptations.note: The wiki's Monster Hunt page lists the boss in round 4-5 of the hunt's eight; a boss's Health there follows the round. Here the tier comes from the printed Health of its hero card (40: tier 3), as family 10's Monster Hunt rows, and the fight's Health is the act curve's.

Grafted Bark (2) copies a minion of either board into the boss's hand as a fresh card of its kind, set to 2/2 and Cost (2) (Petrified, GILA_BOSS_40e); the copy is a generated card, so a minion whose card the run's generation filter keeps from the boss is not a legal choice. Offered only while the hand has room.

Survival of the Fittest (3; the wiki's Monster Hunt table calls it Axe Around): every minion of both boards, in the order they entered play, attacks a random enemy minion, as Mass Hysteria's attacks do (whatever its state; Taunt and Stealth do not matter); each attack's deaths resolve before the next; a minion with no enemy minion left does not attack; the heroes are never attacked. Offered only while both boards hold a minion.

Hack (3), "Deal 1 damage to a minion. Then do it four more times": five hits on the chosen minion, each its own damage event with Spell Damage (the deck's Frothing Berserkers and Armorsmiths count each); the hits stop once it is dead.

The wiki lists a deck of 20 cards. A combat tier fights with 30: the listed cards, a second copy of each non-Legendary single in table order, then the curated fillers named in the row.

Grave Mistake (3), "Trigger all minions' Deathrattles twice": every minion of both boards, in the order they entered play, has each of its Deathrattles (its card's and its enchantments') resolve twice for its own controller, as Feign Death triggers them; a silenced minion's card Deathrattle stays quiet. Offered only while a minion with a Deathrattle is on a board. Grave Mistake the spell (GILA_BOSS_43t, 0 Cost) is the treasure the hunt drops after this fight and is in no deck row; it is scripted and admitted for both sides, and tested from a fixture boss's hand.

Death and Taxes (1) deals the enemy hero one hit of 1 damage for each minion its controller has on the board (a dormant minion and a permanent, such as a dormant run shrine, are not counted: they are not minions an effect can pick). Offered only while the enemy has such a minion.

The wiki (Crooked Pete, Notes): "When Crooked Pete is at 25 Health or less, he transforms into Beastly Pete at the start of his turn. After that: Crooked Pete's deck is replaced by Beastly Pete's; Crooked Pete's hand is removed, then Beastly Pete draws 6 cards; Beastly Pete gains 15 Armor"; the Monster Hunt table: "At 1/2 Health". Here: a script form (GILA_BOSS_52h2 with Beast Within, GILA_BOSS_52p2) entered by Soot Up's start-of-turn trigger when Pete's Health is half his maximum or less (the act curve's maximum, so the threshold scales with it). He keeps his Health and maximum (not the portrait's printed 50), his hand goes to the set-aside zone, Beastly Pete's list replaces his deck and he draws 6 from it, and he gains 15 Armor. A Pete killed outright before such a turn start dies, as in the original (the phase-8 design had sketched an on-death form; the wiki's rule is the one implemented).

Soot Up (1) gives a minion of the boss Stealth until his next turn (Covered in Soot); a minion that has Stealth already is not a choice. Beast Within (1 in the client data; 2 in the wiki's table) gives the boss's minions +1 Attack for good (Beast Mode).

Unfinished Business (2) summons three 1/1 Wisps (GILA_BOSS_55t), as many as the board has room for. Soul Assimilation (4) destroys the caster's Wisps (every card the client names Wisp, the list EMERALD_DREAM Divination reads: the Wisps of this power, Wispering Woods and Wisps of the Old Gods among them), lets their deaths resolve, then takes control of one random enemy minion per Wisp destroyed (one taken while the caster's board is full is destroyed, the engine's control rule; a run shrine never changes sides).

The wiki: "This boss plays a deck identical to the player's." Flag mirrorDeck: the boss's deck is a copy of the run deck as this fight plays it, less the cards the admission table does not admit for a boss (DungeonRun.ApplyEncounter); the row's own deck, a curated Rogue list of basic and classic cards (the hero's class) the wiki does not give, is used only when fewer than 10 such cards remain.

A New Face (0) transforms a minion of either board into a random scripted minion whose Cost is its card's Cost + 2 (any class, behind the run's generation filter for the side that controls it); a minion with no such minion is not a choice. A run shrine chosen is destroyed instead and goes dormant, as from any transform.

Desecrate (1) deals 1 damage to every minion of both boards (a hero power: no Spell Damage); when a hit leaves one dead, the power is readied again after the use (its own Inspire trigger, as Darius Crowley's Fire! is), so each use still costs its Mana. Offered only while a minion is on a board.

Shallow Graves (9), "Summon 7 random minions that died this game": fresh minions of up to seven random deaths of either player this game (one per death; the graveyards are public), for the caster, while its board has room. A dead run shrine (ShrineRules.IsCorpse), a permanent and a card the run's generation filter keeps from the caster are never summoned.

Three Ogres of the wiki's list are collectible cards with no script in this engine (Ogre Ninja, Ogre Brute, Mogor's Champion: the 50% wrong-target Ogres no phase 8 family scripts). Curated replacements, as for Grubb in family 10: Stranglethorn Tiger, Ogre Magi and Hungry Ettin.

Terrify (4; 3 in the wiki's table) shuffles a minion of either board into its own controller's deck through the engine's MoveToDeck, as Recycle's returns are (the card itself, reset as that task resets it: its damage gone), and then makes it cost (4) less there (Terrified, GILA_BOSS_58e). A minion whose owner's deck is full is not a choice. A run shrine chosen is destroyed instead and goes dormant (ShrineRules.InterceptLeave); it never enters a deck.

The wiki's Monster Hunt page lists the boss in round 5 of the hunt's eight; a boss's Health there follows the round. Here the tier comes from the printed Health of its hero card (50: tier 4), as family 10's Monster Hunt rows, and the fight's Health is the act curve's.

Cull the Meek (1) destroys a minion with the lowest Attack among the minions of both boards an effect can pick; a tie is broken by the game RNG. The wiki marks it auto-cast; here the boss's AI chooses when to pay for it, as family 08's Ixlid and family 10's Sazzmi, and it is offered only while a minion is on a board.
